newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Defiance Mills looks to interim div.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Defiance Mills looks to interim div.

text.p: Flour miller and baker Defiance Mills said on Friday it looked forward to the resumption of a dividend payment at the end of the first half of the current financial year to June 30, 1997.
Earlier, Defiance posted a 26 percent lower year net profit of A$3.38 million for the year to June 30, 1996 and said it would not post a final dividend.
"The directors believe it prudent not to recommend a final dividend on ordinary shares," Defiance said in releasing the results.
"They are confident that their expectations for improved performance will be realised and look forward to the resumption of dividends at the half year," it said.
Defiance Chairman Thomas O'Brien said in the results statement he was disappointed with the profit, which had been affected by record-high grain prices.
"Defiance incurred an additional A$12 million cost in grain purchases over the previous year," O'Brien said.

"Nevertheless there is cause for optimism for Defiance in the future in light of its performance in extremely competitive markets throughout Australian and New Zealand baking and milling industries which were characterised by overcapacity and price discounting," he said.

A large wheat crop was likely to be harvested in Australia and this may benefit the milling operation with lower wheat costs, particularly given international prices were falling from their record levels, Defiance said.
Defiance Mills' shares were untraded at 3.15 pm (0515 GMT), having closed unchanged at A$1.20 on Thursday.
